hook: You don't have a traffic problem. You have a stewardship problem.
direction: Reframe conversion as stewardship — a category this audience already thinks in. Doubling your conversion rate doubles results from attention you already earned, without spending another dollar. Wasting existing visitors is the leak to fix first.

facebook.text:
You don't have a traffic problem. You have a stewardship problem.

Most churches, nonprofits, and small businesses spend money driving people to their website — then let those visitors walk away without doing anything.

Doubling your conversion rate doubles your results from attention you already earned. No ad spend. No new content. No algorithm to chase.

The leak isn't at the top of the funnel. It's in the middle, where real visitors are landing on pages that don't ask, don't guide, and don't convert.

Fix the leak first. That's stewardship.

instagram.text:
You don't have a traffic problem. You have a stewardship problem.

People are already finding you. The question is what happens next.

Doubling your conversion rate doubles your results — from the same visitors, the same pages, the same attention you already earned.

Wasting that is the leak worth fixing first. Before the next campaign. Before the next post. Before you spend another dollar on reach.

Steward what you have.
